title: Proper pushforward on equivariant coherent Grothendieck groups
statement: For an affine finite-type group scheme $G$ over a field $F$ [def-weil-field, def-sc-group-scheme] acting on an $F$-scheme $Y$ [def-pc-scheme], a $G$-linearized coherent module means a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent] with an isomorphism $a^*\mathcal M\simeq\operatorname{pr}_2^*\mathcal M$ on $G\times_FY$, satisfying the identity and cocycle identities; its geometric fibre action is from $y$ to $gy$. Let $G_0^G(Y)$ be the abelian group on isomorphism classes of these modules, with relations $[\mathcal M]=[\mathcal M']+[\mathcal M'']$ for every equivariant short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal M'\to\mathcal M\to\mathcal M''\to0$. Let $R(G)$ be the analogous group of finite-dimensional rational $G$-modules, with multiplication induced by tensor product. Rational means a counital coassociative coaction $V\to V\otimes_FF[G]$. Tensoring a sheaf with the trivial vector bundle associated to such a module makes $G_0^G(Y)$ an $R(G)$-module. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $F$-schemes with $G$-actions and let $f:X\to Y$ be a $G$-equivariant proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For every $G$-linearized coherent $\mathcal M$ on $X$, the Zariski higher direct images $R^qf_*\mathcal M$ are coherent, carry natural $G$-linearizations, and vanish for $q\gg0$. The formula $f_*[\mathcal M]=\sum_{q\ge0}(-1)^q[R^qf_*\mathcal M]$ defines an $R(G)$-linear homomorphism $G_0^G(X)\to G_0^G(Y)$. These homomorphisms satisfy $(g\circ f)_*=g_*f_*$ for composable equivariant proper morphisms of separated finite-type $F$-schemes, and commute with restriction of the action to a closed subgroup scheme. For $Y=\operatorname{Spec}F$, the groups $H^q(X,\mathcal M)$ are finite-dimensional rational $G$-modules and this pushforward is their alternating class in $R(G)$. For a closed immersion, it is the class of ordinary extension by zero.

proof.text: Since a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0,F$), the finite-type schemes $X,Y$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. They are quasi-compact, and $f$ is quasi-compact and separated because it is proper. Apply [lem-pc-coherent-hi] to $f,\mathcal M$: every $R^qf_*\mathcal M$ is coherent and the higher images vanish globally for large $q$, since $Y$ is quasi-compact. This proves finiteness of the alternating sum before adding an action. A single bound for all quasi-coherent inputs can also be obtained by a finite cover of $Y$ using [lem-pc-local-uniform-higher-direct-image-bound].

Put $f_G=1_G\times f$, and denote projection and action on a $G$-scheme $Z$ by $p_Z,a_Z:G\times_F Z\to Z$. Both squares $(p_X,p_Y,f_G,f)$ and $(a_X,a_Y,f_G,f)$ are Cartesian: in the second, a point $(g,y,x)$ with $gy=f(x)$ corresponds to $(g,g^{-1}x)$. Projection is flat: on affine charts it is extension $B\to F[G]\otimes_F B$, a free $B$-module after choosing an $F$-basis of $F[G]$. Action is projection after the isomorphism $(g,z)\mapsto(g,gz)$, whose inverse uses $g^{-1}$. The same statements hold for $G^r$ and for any closed subgroup $H$, even when nonreduced. These formulas are morphisms of schemes, by the group and action identities, and establish Cartesianity and flatness without a test only on geometric points.

source.place: Tag 02KH, flatness hypotheses for the two action/projection squares; group-action diagram calculation

proof.text: Using the derived adjunctions [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint] and [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition], form on all $D^+$ the same unit/composition mate as in the canonical derived exchange $\beta_b:Lb^*Rf_*K\to Rf'_*Lb_X^*K$ of [def-pc-derived-base-change-map]. For either flat map $b=p_Y,a_Y$, both pullbacks are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-pullback-exact-pushforward-injective], and are their termwise derived functors by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. For $K=N[0]$ with $N$ quasi-coherent, its degree-$q$ cohomology map is precisely the canonical map of [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom]; negative cohomology is zero. Thus $\beta_b$ is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. The same holds for bounded $K$ with quasi-coherent cohomology: apply the finite Postnikov induction of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-postnikov-isomorphism] to the two sides of $\beta_b$. The functors are triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] and [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Exchange commutes with shifts and triangles because its resolution-level unit and counit maps commute with the differentials and with the cone maps. The canonical exact-pullback cohomology identifications are those of [lem-pur-exact-derived-cohomology-coherence]. This applies in particular to $\mathcal M[0]$ and later to $Rf_*\mathcal M$.

Write $\theta:p_X^*\mathcal M\to a_X^*\mathcal M$ for the fibre-action direction of the given linearization, taking the inverse if its supplied direction is $a_X^*\to p_X^*$. Define on $K=Rf_*\mathcal M$ the isomorphism
$$\Theta=\beta_{a_Y}^{-1}\circ R(f_G)_*(\theta)\circ\beta_{p_Y}:p_Y^*K\longrightarrow a_Y^*K.$$
The pullback compositors are unital and associative by [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition]. Apply the two pasting identities of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to the projection/action squares. On $G\times G\times Y$, the maps induced by $\Theta_{g,hy}\Theta_{h,y}$ and $\Theta_{gh,y}$ are the images of $\theta_{g,hx}\theta_{h,x}$ and $\theta_{gh,x}$ under the SAME outer exchange. The middle exchange and its inverse cancel, and the input cocycle equates the remaining coefficient maps. At $e\times Y$, the identity mate is the identity, so $\Theta_e=1$. Pasting is valid for arbitrary maps, including $e$ and multiplication; no flatness of those maps is needed. Therefore $\Theta$ is a genuine derived linearization, natural in equivariant coefficient maps.

source.place: Tags 0ATM (remark-compose-base-change-horizontal), 08HY; mate pasting fills the omitted verification

proof.text: Exactness of $p_Y^*,a_Y^*$ identifies $H^q(\Theta)$ with an isomorphism $p_Y^*R^qf_*\mathcal M\to a_Y^*R^qf_*\mathcal M$; the normalized comparisons respect composites by [lem-pur-exact-derived-cohomology-coherence]. Taking cohomology in the identity and cocycle equalities gives the required sheaf linearizations. For an equivariant short exact sequence, form its triangle, apply the triangulated $Rf_*$, and take the long exact sequence of [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. The construction of $\Theta$ is a morphism of these triangles, including the shifted last arrow, as in step 3. Hence every map of the long exact sequence, including its connecting maps, is equivariant. Kernels and images carry the restricted linearizations because the two flat pullbacks preserve kernels and cokernels; their coherence follows from [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth].

For any finite exact sequence of equivariant coherent sheaves $0\to A_0\to\cdots\to A_n\to0$, put $I_j=\operatorname{im}(A_{j-1}\to A_j)$ and $I_0=I_{n+1}=0$. Then $[A_j]=[I_j]+[I_{j+1}]$ by the defining short-exact-sequence relation, so $\sum_j(-1)^j[A_j]=0$ by cancellation. Apply this to the finite long exact sequence of step 5 (all its tails vanish by step 1). It gives $\chi_f(\mathcal M)=\chi_f(\mathcal M')+\chi_f(\mathcal M'')$. Naturality also gives invariance under equivariant isomorphism. The generators-and-relations definition of $G_0^G$ therefore yields the stated group homomorphism. Tensoring an equivariant coherent sheaf with a finite-dimensional rational module is a finite direct sum on underlying sheaves; it is coherent and exact in either variable. Associativity and unit of tensor make the stated $R(G)$-action well defined on the relations.

source.place: Tag 01Y0; elementary cancellation in the generators-and-relations group

proof.text:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional rational $G$-module. The bilinear map on sections $v\otimes s\mapsto v\otimes s$ induces
$$V\otimes_F R^qf_*\mathcal M\longrightarrow R^qf_*(V\otimes_F\mathcal M).$$
Choose a basis of $V$: the map becomes the direct-sum comparison for finitely many copies of $R^qf_*$ and is an isomorphism, since finite sums of resolutions compute finite sums of derived images. Its construction is natural in both $V$ and $\mathcal M$. To check the linearizations, pass to $G\times Y$ using the exchange of step 3. If the universal group element has matrix $(c_{ij})$ on $V$, both routes send $v_j\otimes z$ to $\sum_i c_{ij}v_i\otimes\Theta(z)$; $R(f_G)_*$ is $\mathcal O_{G\times Y}$-linear, so the coefficients $c_{ij}\in F[G]$ can be pulled outside it. Thus the isomorphism is equivariant over the whole group scheme. Taking alternating classes gives $\chi_f(V\otimes\mathcal M)=[V]\chi_f(\mathcal M)$, and additivity gives $R(G)$-linearity for virtual modules.

source.place: Tag 02KH; finite-free tensor comparison by an explicit basis computation

proof.text:
For composable $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$, let $K=Rf_*\mathcal M$. It has bounded coherent cohomology by step 1; $Rg_*K$ and the direct images of its finitely many truncations have bounded coherent cohomology by [lem-pc-noetherian-proper-bounded-coherent-image]. On bounded derived categories the flat pullbacks $p_Y^*,a_Y^*$ are t-exact. Consequently they preserve the WHOLE canonical truncation triangles, with their last arrows, by [lem-pod-texact-truncation-triangle-comparison]. Functoriality of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] applies to the derived isomorphism $\Theta$. Thus the triangle $\tau_{\le q-1}K\to\tau_{\le q}K\to H^q(K)[-q]\to$ carries compatible actions. Apply $Rg_*$ and step 3 to obtain compatible actions on its image triangle. The long exact cohomology sequence is equivariant; the same finite image cancellation as step 6 gives
$$\chi(Rg_*\tau_{\le q}K)=\chi(Rg_*\tau_{\le q-1}K)+(-1)^q\chi_g(H^qK).$$
Here $\chi(L)=\sum_i(-1)^i[H^iL]$ with the induced linearizations; shifts give the displayed sign. Summing from the first to the last nonzero cohomology degree telescopes to $\chi(Rg_*K)=\sum_q(-1)^q\chi_g(R^qf_*\mathcal M)$.

source.place: Canonical finite truncation argument in place of relative Leray, Tag 01F6 (lemma-relative-Leray); finite Euler cancellation

proof.text:
The canonical isomorphism $\rho:R(gf)_*\mathcal M\simeq Rg_*Rf_*\mathcal M$ is [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition]. For each of the action and projection squares, [lem-sfb-derived-base-change-vertical-pasting] gives the equality
$$\rho'\beta^{\mathrm{out}}=Rg'_*\beta^{\mathrm{top}}\circ\beta^{\mathrm{bottom}}\circ b^*\rho.$$
All its quasi-compact/quasi-separated hypotheses hold for $f,g$; the intermediate $Rf_*\mathcal M$ is quasi-coherent in cohomology by step 1. Substitute this equality for both exchange factors in step 4: the intervening factors cancel, leaving exactly the iterated action on $Rg_*Rf_*\mathcal M$. Naturality in the coefficient map $\theta$ identifies the middle factors. Hence $\rho$ is equivariant. Taking cohomology and applying step 8 yields $\chi_{gf}(\mathcal M)=g_*f_*[\mathcal M]$, proving composition on generators and therefore on the group.

Let $j:H\hookrightarrow G$ be a closed subgroup. The underlying coherent sheaf and its higher direct images do not change on restriction. To identify their linearizations, pull the formula for $\Theta$ back along $j\times Y$ and apply mate pasting to the square of $j\times X,j\times Y$ and $f_H,f_G$. The identities $p_G(j\times Y)=p_H$ and $a_G(j\times Y)=a_H$ identify the outer exchanges with the $H$-exchanges. Although $j$ need not be flat, derived pullback gives exactly these identities by [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition]. Both $p_H,a_H$ are flat by step 2, so the two resulting endpoints compute ordinary pullback and its cohomology; the derived middle exchange is invertible because its composite with the invertible $G$-exchange is the invertible $H$-exchange. The coefficient map becomes the restricted $\theta$. The same cancellation as in step 4 therefore yields $L(j\times Y)^*\Theta_G=\Theta_H$ in the derived category. To pass to the sheaf linearizations although $u=j\times Y$ is not flat, fix $q$ and put $A=\tau_{\le q}Lp_G^*K$, $B=\tau_{\le q}La_G^*K$, which have no cohomology above $q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-pullback-top-cohomology] the comparisons $\kappa_{u,A},\kappa_{u,B}$ identify $H^q(Lu^*A),H^q(Lu^*B)$ with $u^*H^q(A)=u^*p_G^*R^qf_*\mathcal M$ and $u^*a_G^*R^qf_*\mathcal M$, naturally for the morphism $\tau_{\le q}\Theta_G:A\to B$, and compatibly with the composition $p_G\circ u=p_H$ (resp. $a_G\circ u=a_H$). Since $Lu^*Lp_G^*K\simeq Lp_H^*K$ and $p_H$ is flat, $Lu^*$ of $\tau_{\ge q+1}Lp_G^*K$ has no cohomology in degrees $\le q$, so $H^q(Lu^*A)\to H^q(Lu^*Lp_G^*K)$ is an isomorphism, and likewise for $B$. Hence $H^q(\Theta_H)=u^*H^q(\Theta_G)$ under the ordinary composition isomorphisms $u^*p_G^*\simeq p_H^*$, $u^*a_G^*\simeq a_H^*$: the $H$-linearization of $R^qf_*\mathcal M$ is the restriction of its $G$-linearization. Alternating classes prove restriction compatibility. This argument also applies to $e:\operatorname{Spec}F\to G$, justifying the identity check without assuming $e$ flat.

source.place: Tags 0ATM and 08HY; arbitrary-map pasting between the two flat outer base changes

proof.text: For $Y=\operatorname{Spec}F$, [lem-pc-coherent-hi] makes $H^q(X,\mathcal M)$ finite-dimensional and zero for large $q$. Apply [lem-sfb-linearized-qcoherent-cohomology-coaction], whose hypotheses hold because $X$ is quasi-compact and separated and $\mathcal M$ is quasi-coherent. It gives counital coassociative rational coactions and the usual action $s(y)\mapsto\theta_{g,g^{-1}y}s(g^{-1}y)$, including connecting-map compatibility. Its canonical flat-base-change identification is the same as the one used in steps 3--4, so these are the cohomological actions already constructed. Finally modules over $\operatorname{Spec}F$ are vector spaces: the two pullbacks to affine $G$ identify a linearization with the matrix of a coaction into $V\otimes_F F[G]$; the cocycle and identity are respectively coassociativity and the counit. Thus $G_0^G(\operatorname{Spec}F)=R(G)$ and the pushforward is exactly the alternating rational cohomology class.

source.place: Tags 02O5, 02O6, 02KH; the existing universal-group-element coaction lemma

proof.text: If $f=i$ is a closed immersion, it is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc]. Hence [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hi] gives $R^qi_*\mathcal M=0$ for $q>0$. Only $i_*\mathcal M$ remains, with its natural action from step 4. Its sections on an open $U\subseteq Y$ are $\mathcal M(i^{-1}U)$ by the definition of module direct image; on the complement of the closed image all stalks are zero, and on the image they are the original stalks with the restricted scalar action. This is the ordinary extension by zero along a closed immersion. Therefore $i_*[\mathcal M]=[i_*\mathcal M]$ as asserted.
